title: IBD Flare Timeline
description: Illustrative 12-month model of Crohn's disease after diagnosis. Learners place events (starting steroids, starting a biologic, missed biologic doses, a gut infection, a stressful exam week) on a timeline and compare how gut inflammation, symptoms, energy, and mood respond. Not a prediction for any real person.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: neuroscience (gut-brain axis)
publisher: Gut Check: The Neuroscience of How Your Gut and Brain Talk
learningObjectives: Relate gut inflammation, symptoms, energy, and mood over time in inflammatory bowel disease.
Analyze how steroids, a biologic, and missed doses change inflammation and symptoms on different time scales.
Distinguish events that change symptoms and mood (such as exam stress) from events that change inflammation (such as missed doses or infection).
keyQuestions: Why can symptoms improve before inflammation has fully settled?
Why are steroids used only as a short-term bridge?
What happens to inflammation after maintenance doses are missed, and how quickly?
Which events change mood and symptoms without changing inflammation?
misconceptions: Feeling better means the gut has fully healed.
Once someone is in remission, they can stop their medicine.
Stress is the cause of IBD flares.
IBD only affects the gut and has nothing to do with energy or mood.
